posts.title: Using a second number for sign-ups and verification codes
posts.excerpt: Every app, shop and loyalty card wants your phone number. Here’s how a second number keeps your personal one off marketing lists and data leaks.
posts.content:
Newsletters, delivery apps, free trials, store loyalty cards — almost every sign-up form now asks for a phone number. Each one is another company holding your personal number, and another place it can leak from. A second phone number gives those forms a number to use without handing over the one your family and bank rely on.

Why your phone number is worth protecting

Your phone number follows you for years. It links your accounts together, it’s often used to recover passwords, and once it’s on a marketing list it tends to stay there. When a company you signed up with is breached, your number can end up in spam and scam lists you never agreed to.

  • Fewer spam calls and texts on the number you actually answer.
  • Less tracking across shops and apps that match customers by phone number.
  • Easy to walk away: block senders on your second number without touching your personal line.

Where a second number works well

Use your second number anywhere you’d rather not give out your real one:

  • Online shopping accounts and delivery apps
  • Free trials and newsletter sign-ups
  • Wi-Fi hotspots, store loyalty cards and raffles
  • Classified ads and marketplace listings
  • Dating apps and new contacts you haven’t met yet

When to keep using your personal number

Some services only accept numbers from a mobile carrier, and some send codes from short numbers that internet-based numbers may not receive. For your bank, government services, and the account you use to recover your email, keep your personal number. Those are the accounts where losing a code would hurt most.

Tip: Before you switch an important account to a new number, make sure you can receive a test code on it.

How to set it up

  1. Download Wi-Fi Calling & Texting and create your account.
  2. Choose a US or Canadian number by city.
  3. Use that number the next time a form asks for a phone number.
  4. If a sender starts spamming you, block them from the conversation menu.

Texts to your second number arrive in the Messages tab, over Wi-Fi or mobile data. See how texting from your second number works, or how to block numbers you don’t want to hear from.

The bottom line

Give your second number to the companies you don’t fully trust, and keep your personal number for the people and accounts that matter. It takes a couple of minutes to set up and saves a lot of spam later.

posts.title: Wi-Fi calling vs cellular calls: what’s the difference?
posts.excerpt: Wi-Fi calls travel over the internet instead of your carrier’s network. Here’s what that means for cost, quality and calling from places with weak signal.
posts.content:
A cellular call goes from your phone to a mobile tower and across your carrier’s network. A Wi-Fi call goes over the internet instead — through your home router, an office network or a café hotspot. To the person you’re talking to it sounds like any other call, but it changes where and how you can call.

The main differences

Cellular callWi-Fi call
NeedsMobile signalWi-Fi or mobile data
Works in basements and thick buildingsOften poorYes, if the Wi-Fi is good
Works abroadRoaming planAny Wi-Fi connection
Uses your carrier minutesYesNo

When Wi-Fi calling is the better choice

  • Weak signal at home or work. Thick walls and basements block mobile signal, but your Wi-Fi still reaches.
  • Travelling. Connect to hotel Wi-Fi and keep calling without a roaming plan.
  • Calling friends on the same app. App-to-app calls are free.

What affects Wi-Fi call quality

Call quality depends on your connection. A stable network matters more than a fast one: crowded public hotspots and weak signal at the edge of your Wi-Fi range cause most problems.

Tip: If a call starts breaking up, move closer to the router or switch to mobile data — the app works over both.

Calling over Wi-Fi with a second number

Wi-Fi Calling & Texting gives you a second US or Canadian number that works entirely over Wi-Fi or data. Calls to friends who use the app are free, and you can call any regular number using coins.

The bottom line

Cellular calls are great when signal is strong. Wi-Fi calling fills the gaps: weak indoor coverage, trips abroad and free calls with friends.

posts.title: How to call any landline or mobile with coins
posts.excerpt: Calling someone who isn’t on the app? Coins let you dial regular landlines and mobiles from your second number. Here’s how coins work.
posts.content:
Free app-to-app calls are great, but plenty of people you need to reach — a doctor’s office, a hotel, a relative without a smartphone — only have a regular number. Coins let you call them from your second number.

What you need

  • An active Lite or Pro subscription
  • Your own second number from the app
  • Coins in your balance

How coins work

Coins pay for calls and texts to regular phone numbers. US calls are roughly one coin per minute, and texts to US numbers are about one coin each. Calls and chats with app users never use coins.

Tip: See the exact cost for every country in Settings → Purchase Coins → Add coins → See per-minute charges.

Making a call

  1. Open the Dial screen and make sure “Phone Calls” is selected.
  2. Pick the country, then type the number or choose a contact from your phonebook.
  3. Tap the call button. The call goes out from your second number.

Calling abroad

Choose the country on the dial pad’s country picker, then dial the number without its leading zero. Our international calling guides show the format for popular countries.

Topping up

Check your balance in Settings → Purchase Coins and top up whenever you need to. There’s no subscription for coins — buy them only when you use them.

The bottom line

Use free app calls for friends on the app, and coins for everyone else. Read more about calling any phone number.

posts.title: Selling online? Use a second number with buyers
posts.excerpt: Marketplace buyers need a way to reach you, but they don’t need your personal number. Here’s how a second number keeps selling safe and simple.
posts.content:
Listing a sofa, a bike or old electronics usually means sharing a phone number with strangers. Most buyers are genuine, but your number stays with every one of them long after the sale. A second number lets buyers reach you without giving them your personal line.

Why sellers use a second number

  • Privacy: strangers never see your personal number.
  • Organisation: every buyer conversation lives in one place.
  • Easy exit: block time-wasters without changing your real number.

Safer selling tips

  1. Put your second number in the listing, not your personal one.
  2. Keep the conversation in the app until you agree on a meeting.
  3. Meet in a public place for local pickups.
  4. Never share codes sent to your phone — no genuine buyer needs one.

Tip: A buyer asking you to read out a code sent to your phone is a common scam. Stop the conversation and block the number.

Handling lots of buyers

If you sell regularly, Pro features help: send one update to many people with broadcast messages, or let callers leave a message with voicemail.

The bottom line

A second number costs less than the hassle of spam and strangers on your personal line. See how online sellers use it.

posts.excerpt: Moving a chat off the dating app means sharing a number. Give matches a second number instead and keep your personal one until you’re ready.
posts.content:
Sooner or later, a good match asks for your number. Sharing it feels like a big step — once someone has your personal number, you can’t take it back. A second number lets you keep talking without giving that away.

Why a second number makes sense

  • You stay in control of who has your personal number.
  • Blocking is instant and doesn’t affect your real line.
  • Less linking: your personal number is often tied to social accounts that someone could find.

A simple routine

  1. Share your second number when you move off the dating app.
  2. Call or text from the app until you feel comfortable.
  3. Share your personal number only when you’re ready — or never.

Tip: Video call a match before meeting. Video calls between app users are free, and a quick call confirms they’re who they say they are.

Extra privacy with Pro

Turn on anonymous calling and the person you call won’t see your number at all. It’s included with the Pro plan.

If things go wrong

Open the conversation and choose Block from the menu. Blocked numbers can’t call or text you again. Learn more about blocking numbers.

The bottom line

Your personal number is yours to share when you choose. See how a second number helps with dating.

posts.title: How to block spam calls and texts on your second number
posts.excerpt: Spam calls and texts are annoying, but stopping them takes seconds. Here’s how to block a number, review your blocked list and unblock someone.
posts.content:
Once a number is on a few marketing lists, spam follows. The good news: on your second number, blocking takes seconds, and a blocked number can’t call or text you again.

Block from a conversation

  1. Open the conversation with the number you want to block.
  2. Tap the menu in the top corner.
  3. Choose Block.

That’s it. The number can no longer call or text your second number.

Review and unblock numbers

Changed your mind? Go to Settings → Call Settings → Blocked numbers to see everyone you’ve blocked, and tap Unblock next to a number to let them reach you again.

Tip: Never call back a missed call from an unknown international number. Some scams rely on you calling an expensive number.

Cut spam at the source

  • Use your second number for sign-ups and listings, and keep your personal number private.
  • Don’t reply to spam texts — even “STOP” can confirm your number is active.
  • Never share codes sent to your phone with anyone who calls or texts you.

The bottom line

Blocking keeps your second number clean, and using it for sign-ups keeps your personal number out of spam lists. Read more about blocking numbers.

posts.excerpt: Your second number isn’t stuck on your phone. Sign in on the web to call, text and chat from your computer with the same account.
posts.content:
Typing long messages on a phone is slow, and taking calls at your desk is easier with a headset. The Wi-Fi Calling & Texting web app puts your second number in your browser, so you can call and text from your computer.

What you can do on the web

  • Call regular numbers and friends on the app
  • Send and read texts and chats
  • See your call history and contacts
  • Manage your settings and devices

It’s the same account as the iPhone app, so your number, messages, calls and contacts are there when you sign in.

Getting started

  1. Open the web app in your browser — there’s nothing to install.
  2. Sign in with the same phone number you use in the app.
  3. Allow microphone access when your browser asks, so you can make calls.

Tip: Use headphones with a microphone for the clearest calls from your computer.

Keep your account secure

Signed in on a shared computer? Go to Settings → Account Settings → My Devices to see where you’re signed in and sign out other devices.

The bottom line

Use the app on the go and the web app at your desk — it’s the same number either way. Read more about the web app.

faqs.answer: Yes. Sign in to the web app with the same account to call and text from your computer.

faqs.question: Which numbers can I choose?
faqs.answer: You can choose a number from the United States or Canada.

cta.title: Get your second number today
cta.description: Call and text over Wi-Fi from a real US or Canadian number, on the phone you already own.
